Despite Mac shipments falling 11% in Q3 2026, Apple's market share rose from 8.5% to 9.5%, as the overall market saw shipments plunge 20.1%. IDC's latest report offers the following details.

Apple outperforms most of the PC market in a challenging environment

IDC today released a report on global PC shipments for Q3 2026, noting that while Apple's Mac shipments declined compared to a year ago, its performance far outpaced the overall market.

According to IDC's preliminary data, Apple shipped a total of 5.9 million Macs in Q3 2026, down 11.3% from 6.7 million in the same period last year.

However, the overall PC market saw an even steeper decline, with global shipments falling 20.1% year-over-year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

Apple thus held steady in fourth position, trailing Lenovo (leading with 14.9 million shipments and 23.8% market share), HP (10.3 million shipments, 16.5% share), and Dell (7.6 million shipments, 12.1% share).

Among the top five vendors, HP saw the largest year-over-year decline, with shipments falling 30.9%. ASUS posted the smallest decline, down 8.6% year-over-year, with shipments of 5.5 million and a market share of 8.7%.

Looking ahead, IDC said, "channel concerns about high inventory and weak demand at elevated price points may drive promotional activity in the near term," adding that "pricing will still remain well above year-ago levels."

The firm also noted that the economy has weakened since last quarter, which could further dampen demand and "cast a shadow over the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and 2027."
